newsitem.title: USA: IMC sees continued good demand for products.
newsitem.headline: IMC sees continued good demand for products.

text.p: IMC Global Inc, which produces and markets phosphate and potash crop nutrients and animal feed ingredients, said Friday it is optimistic that demand for its products will remain strong for the foreseeable future.
"The near- and long-term fundamentals for IMC Global remain very attractive," Robert Fowler Jr., president, said in a statement.

He said near-term demand is expected to come from a robust summer fill program for phosphate and potash now underway, continued strong international demand particularly from China and India, and heavy applications of crop nutrients this fall.

"In addition, even with good crop yields in North America later this year, world grain stocks will likely remain near historicallly low levels," Fowler said. "This will further encourage the use of fertilizers to increase crop production and should create opportunities for another strong season next spring."

With the world population growing at an annual rate of nearly 90 million and improving diets in developing countries demanding greater use of feed grains, the market for crop nutrients will undoubtedly continue to grow, he added.

Earlier, IMC reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.93 a share before a $0.03 charge, up from $0.71 a year ago. For the full year, it earned $2.15 a share before a $0.12 charge, compared with $2.31 a share. Net earnings after special charges for fiscal 1996 were $144.3 million or $1.56 a share.

Among IMC Global's five business units, only IMC-Agrico Cro Nutrients reported lower net sales in the fourth quarter. Despite increased sales volumes, net sales at this unit declined four percent primarily due to lower average prices for concentrated phosphate crop nutrients.

Fowler said the company's cost-reduction program was exceeding expectations with more than $43.0 million in pretax cost savings achieved during the past year. Cumulative cost savings from the March 1996 IMC/Vigoro merger were estimated at $120 million pretax over three years. First year savings, however, were greater than anticipated, Fowler said, and it appears likely the original $120 million cost-reduction target will be exceeded.
